title: Verification flow
description: Schema for a *.verification.flow.json artifact: an executable-by-a-human-or-agent specification of the checks that prove a mechanism is LIVE rather than decorative. Distinct from docs/product-truth/schemas/flow.schema.json, which describes user journeys (steps, screens, entities, acceptance_scenarios) and has no field for a runnable command, an observable pass criterion, a negative control, or an observed current state. A verification flow is not a journey: its unit is a falsifiable check with an exit code, not a step a user takes. Every check MUST carry a `currently` block whose evidence quotes the real output of a command that was actually run; a fabricated `passing` is a schema-legal but process-fatal lie, so `unverified` is provided as an honest escape hatch.

$schema.description: Path or URI of this schema, so the artifact is self-describing.

id.description: <product>/<name>, path-stable. Mirrors the product-truth id convention.

component.description: Kebab-case component id (docs/components index) this flow verifies.

subject.description: WHAT this flow verifies and WHICH failure mode it exists to catch.

mechanism.description: The machinery under verification, in one line.

failure_mode_guarded.description: The specific way this machinery could be decorative — the thing a green check must rule out.

prior_incidents.description: Named past occurrences of the failure mode in this repo. Grounds the flow in history rather than theory.

summary.description: HUMAN: one-paragraph plain-language description of what a fully-green run of this flow would prove.

repo_root.description: Absolute path the commands in this flow are written against.

observed_at.description: The exact repo state every `currently` value was measured against. Without this the states rot silently.

working_tree_dirty.description: Paths modified but uncommitted at observation time. A check measured against a dirty path is measuring in-flight work, not the committed contract — record it here or the evidence is unreproducible.

angle_vocabulary.description: The taxonomy this flow both USES (to classify its own checks) and VERIFIES (as the mechanism under test).

core.description: Angle id -> one-line definition. Keys are constrained to the $defs/angle enum so a flow cannot declare a vocabulary its own checks are unable to reference.

cap.description: Maximum angles chargeable to a single AC.

rollup.description: DERIVED count of checks by `currently.state`. Regenerate rather than hand-edit.

angle.description: Which angle of the machinery a check verifies. criterion = the literal claim holds; reachability = the real production entry point produces the behaviour AND its result is consumed in control flow; seam = real producer output fed into the real consumer; real_artifact = the actual on-disk artifact, not a hand-authored fixture; deployed = the built/deployed copy, not the source tree; boundary/failure = conditional edge angles.

intent.description: What this phase, fully green, establishes that the previous phase did not.

gate_rule.description: Optional rule for whether later phases may be trusted while this one is red.

id.description: Stable check id, VC-<phase>.<n>. Never renumber a check; retire it with status instead.

modifiers.description: must_block marks a check whose subject is a gate/guard/validator, so a paired negative control is mandatory and must be shown to BLOCK.

claim.description: The single falsifiable statement under test. One claim per check — a compound claim cannot be falsified cleanly.

entry_point.description: The real production way in that this check invokes (CLI, hook, workflow dispatch, deployed script). NOT an internal helper import.

setup_command.description: Optional single simple command run first to produce the artifact `command` inspects. Kept separate so both obey the repo's one-simple-command shell rule (no &&, ;, pipes-to-other-commands, or cd).

command.description: A single, simple, runnable command whose exit code and stdout ARE the verdict. Absolute paths only; stderr redirected to /tmp.

pass_criteria.description: Observable, not vibes: an exit code, an exact string, or a presence assertion in a named generated artifact.

owner_surface.description: Repo-relative path(s) that must change for this check to pass. Empty is never correct: if nothing must change, the check is not falsifiable.

blocks.description: Check ids that cannot be meaningfully evaluated while this one is red.

negative_control.description: The known-bad input that MUST be rejected. A check without one can pass on dead code. Only genuinely non-falsifiable checks (pure census/measurement) may declare not_applicable, and must justify it. A falsifiable control MUST carry its own `currently` block: an unrun control records state `unverified` rather than omitting the block, so 'we never fed it bad input' is visible in the artifact instead of silent.

input.description: The known-bad artifact, record, or invocation fed through the SAME entry point.

command.description: Single simple command that feeds the known-bad input through the entry point.

expected_result.description: The observable rejection: non-zero exit, a specific error string, or absence from the generated artifact.

reason.description: Why no known-bad input is meaningful — e.g. the check is a census with no pass/fail semantics of its own.

currently.description: The CURRENT observed state, with proof. `failing` is expected and useful — the flow doubles as a to-do list. A `passing` state whose evidence does not show the pass is the phantom-done failure this whole taxonomy exists to prevent.

state.description: passing = command run, criteria met. failing = command run, criteria not met. blocked = cannot be run to a meaningful verdict because a prerequisite or the environment prevents it. unverified = not yet run; honest placeholder.

command.description: The command actually run to establish this state. Never empty: an evidence item with no command is an assertion, not evidence.

output.description: Verbatim (or faithfully truncated) real output. Never paraphrased into a claim.

interpretation.description: What the quoted output means for the claim. Kept separate from `output` so the raw evidence stays unedited.
